observations.seen: Frame 1 is labeled 'Golden Hour Look' but renders as a flat, dim purple-blue wash with no warm key light or rim. Frame 3 does have a low directional sun, but the sky behind the buildings is blown out to white.

Frame 2 grounds the players with dark square blob patches on the floor instead of real shadows. Frame 3's long shadows have stair-stepped, pixelated edges from a low-resolution shadow map, most visible beside the bleachers on the left. Frame 1 has only faint contact darkening under the feet.

Only frame 4 shows a wet-floor specular streak and a glossy blue tower. Floors in frames 1 and 3 are fully matte, and frame 2 has only a faint sheen. Nothing appears to pick up environment lighting from an IBL source.

Buildings are plain boxes with repeating, uniform window grids. Bleachers are untextured slabs. The ball cart, ornate lamps and graffiti backboard add some detail, but the backdrops read as placeholder.
Frame 3 has haze, frame 4 has rain streaks and frame 2 has floating dust specks. Frame 1 has no depth haze, so the street scene looks flat.
Court surfaces are flat single-color fills with no wear or roughness variation. Character clothing and skin share the same plastic shading. The trophy in frame 1 is the only convincing metal.
Characters are low-poly with blocky hands and similar silhouettes. Detached white arc shapes float near the players' sneakers in every frame and read as geometry artifacts.

In frame 1 the leftmost player is cut off at the frame edge, the ball is clipped at the right edge, and the subject cluster sits off-balance. In frames 2 to 4 the players are spread evenly with no focal hierarchy.
The camera is a low, roughly 20–30° perspective view close to the players. The recipe's 70° broadcast framing is not present, and the court occupies far more than 25–40% of the frame.
Frame 2 uses depth of field and bloom effectively. Frame 1 shows visible noise and grain, and frame 3 has clipped highlights in the sky gaps. Color grading is inconsistent from scene to scene.
Most players stand in a stiff near-A-pose with arms hanging away from the body. Only the ball handler shows a dribble crouch.
The scoreboard and controls strip are clean and readable. The top bar of mode and court buttons looks like a developer toolbar and crowds the view, and the HUD appears only in frame 1.
